  Readable gloss: "Denotes the mule, the sturdy hybrid of horse and donkey prized across the ancient Near East for reliability on rough terrain. In Scripture the mule is conspicuously royal: Absalom's sons ride mules as a mark of princely status (2 Sam 13:29), and Absalom himself is fatally caught while riding one in battle (2 Sam 18:9). Solomon receives mules as annual tribute (1 Kgs 10:25), and Obadiah searches for pasture for royal mules during drought (1 Kgs 18:5). Mules also appear as pack animals ('the load of a pair of mules,' 2 Kgs 5:17), in Tyrian commerce (Ezek 27:14), and among the livestock of returning exiles (Ezra 2:66). Psalm 32:9 uses the mule as a cautionary image of stubbornness."
